clue.text: He and I condoned my dodgy tax-free dealings?

indicators.note: something dodgy is shady or unreliable, so these letters are not to be trusted in their printed order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that they and an accomplice turned a blind eye to shady untaxed business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' only joins: 'dodgy' rearranges HE, I and CONDONED to HIDDENECONO, and MY stays put at the end. The question mark admits the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: The hidden economy is the black market of cash work and trade kept off the books and away from the taxman.

clue.text: Momentum member occupying fancy suite

indicators.note: one piece occupying another sits inside it, so the member goes within the rearranged suite
fancy as a verb or adjective suggests something elaborated or reworked, so the letters of suite are rearranged

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A member of the Momentum political group takes up residence in a smart hotel suite.
explanation.walkthrough: Momentum is also a left-wing UK Labour campaign group, which makes 'member' look as if it belongs to it. 'fancy' gives IETUS, with the member inside after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus and momentum are both the driving force that keeps something moving forward.

clue.text: Tyrant some Parisian beat up

parts.note: des is French for 'some', as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: to beat a rival is to top them

explanation.surface: A tyrant has some resident of Paris roughed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat up' reads as one phrase meaning assault, but 'beat' gives TOP and 'up' reverses it to POT.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler who wields power cruelly, which is what a tyrant is.

clue.text: Nick cannot choose trousers

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket something, so the answer is pocketed within these words

explanation.surface: A man called Nick cannot make up his mind which trousers to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like a noun, the thing Nick cannot pick, but it is a verb meaning pockets: the answer sits in caNNOT CHoose.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick is a small cut or groove, and so is a notch.

clue.text: Nonces dispersed after tea dances

indicators.note: the scrambled letters come after the tea, so tea comes first in the answer

parts.note: cha (or char) is slang for tea

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered about, so the letters of nonces are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Nonce-words are scattered about once tea is done and the dances begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispersed' produces CONNES; 'after' puts it behind the tea.
explanation.definitionFit: The chaconne is a slow stately dance of Spanish origin, popular in baroque music.

clue.text: Woman, one to write about old boy network?

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the whole string is written backwards

parts.note: Ms is the title for a woman
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
to pen something is to write it

explanation.surface: A woman picks someone to write about the old school-tie network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the subject of', but it reverses MS + I + TO + PEN. The old boy network is the British habit of favouring old schoolmates; the question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouritism to family or friends in handing out jobs, much like the old-school-tie favours of former classmates.

clue.text: God, an incarnation of Vishnu, returning to embrace new country

parts.note: My! and My God! are both exclamations of surprise, so God gives MY

indicators.note: to embrace something is to hold it within, so the new letter goes inside
returning means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Rama is the seventh avatar of the Hindu god Vishnu

explanation.surface: A Hindu deity's incarnation comes back to welcome a new land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'God' looks like Vishnu himself but is only the exclamation. 'returning' turns RAMA into AMAR, and N goes inside after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: Myanmar is the official name of the south-east Asian nation formerly called Burma.

clue.text: Iraqi construction of phonetics translated with cunning

indicators.note: to translate is to change into another form, so the letters of phonetics take a new order

parts.note: arch means knowingly sly or roguish, which is a sense of cunning

explanation.surface: A phonetic transcription gets translated, with some cunning, from an Iraqi text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges PHONETICS into CTESIPHON, the ancient city south-east of Baghdad.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taq Kasra at Ctesiphon in Iraq is a vast ancient brick arch, a famous piece of construction.

clue.text: Without pity, detective dominates inferior in bank

indicators.note: these pieces go in the bank, inside its letters

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it

indicators.note: in a down clue the dominant piece sits above, so the detective goes first

parts.note: Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of Colin Dexter's novels and the TV series
inferior means less, as in of less quality

explanation.surface: A ruthless detective lords it over a junior officer at the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'dominates' means sits on top of, so the detective comes before 'inferior'; both go inside the bank word after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something remorselessly means doing it without regret or mercy, relentlessly.

clue.text: People poetic at heart compose for organ, perhaps?

parts.note: types are people, as in 'all sorts of types'

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters, so the middle of poetic is used

explanation.surface: Poets at heart write music for the church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' looks musical but means a newspaper, a house organ; typesetting arranges the type for printing.
explanation.definitionFit: To typeset is to arrange text in type ready for printing, as a newspaper or periodical is printed.

clue.text: Late exercises stopping at one

indicators.note: a stopping plugs a gap, so the exercises fill a gap within the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
an ace is a one in cards and dice
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Someone's late exercise sessions are stopping at one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' looks like an adjective about time, but it means dead.
explanation.definitionFit: At peace is a gentle euphemism for dead, as the late so-and-so is someone who has died.

clue.text: Not about to cut south, going west by old burial site

indicators.note: by means beside, so the old letter sits next to the rest
the reversed word is set to cut into the other letters, splitting them
going west means being ruined or wrecked, so the letters of south are broken up and rearranged
about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone has no plans to cut south, heading west instead past an ancient grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' (wrecked) makes SUTHO; the reversed word cuts it after its third letter. Sutton Hoo in Suffolk, England, is the Anglo-Saxon ship burial site.
explanation.definitionFit: Sutton Hoo is the seventh-century Anglo-Saxon ship burial ground in Suffolk, famed for its treasure hoard.

clue.text: Work force turning back time

indicators.note: turning back means going in reverse, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police force

explanation.surface: A workforce is turning back the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work force' reads as one word, the staff, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, tempo means the speed or time at which a piece is played.

clue.text: Violent guards in part look here

indicators.note: the guards go in the part, within its letters

parts.note: the SS were the brutal Nazi guard units

explanation.surface: Thuggish guards play a role in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guards' looks like the verb that would put one piece round another, but it is a noun, part of the SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is a whispered call for attention, just as 'look here' tries to get someone's notice.

clue.text: Attention grabbers safe to assume extremely cushy numbers

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, so the ends of cushy are taken
to assume is to take on, so the numbers take the safe word into themselves

parts.note: safe and sure both mean certain, reliable

explanation.surface: Cushy numbers, it seems safe to assume, grab attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to assume' means taking in, so the numbers hold 'safe'; the clue mentions 'safe' first, but the ends of 'cushy' lead the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynosure is a centre of attention or admiration, something that draws every eye.

clue.text: Old racer clever tho' eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre and odd, so these letters are out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vintage racing driver is clever, though rather odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old racer' reads as a person, but it is a car name: Louis Chevrolet raced cars before co-founding the brand, so the name fits both.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Chevrolet was a racing driver of the early twentieth century, and the car marque bears his name.

clue.text: Censor stopping course, reportedly upsetting teacher

indicators.note: a stopping plugs a gap, so the censor fills a gap inside the other word
in a down clue upsetting turns a word upside down, reading it from the bottom

parts.note: course sounds like coarse, which means rude
Cato the Elder was the famous Roman censor

explanation.surface: A censor halts an offensive course, upsetting the teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' means course is heard as coarse, which gives the synonym; 'upsetting' turns it upside down to EDUR, which the Roman censor stops.
explanation.definitionFit: An educator is someone who teaches or instructs others, a formal word for a teacher.

clue.text: Get trim on too much sport in an OTT way

indicators.note: in an across clue a piece on another comes after it

parts.note: over means excessively, too much, as in overdone
to dress is to trim or decorate, to get things neatly dressed

explanation.surface: Getting trim is too much of a sport for someone who goes over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' is the verb meaning wear: to overdress is to wear clothes in an over-the-top way. The blog takes only 'in an OTT way' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdress is to wear clothes too formal or showy for the occasion, flaunting them in excess.

clue.text: India blocking exile, European, to make up for mistake

indicators.note: a piece blocking another sits in its way, inside it

parts.note: an expat lives away from their homeland, as an exile does
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Indian blocks a European exile's bid to atone for a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside EXPAT after its P, and E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To expiate a sin or wrong is to atone for it, making amends.

clue.text: Little boat's deviation from course line

parts.note: a yaw is a ship's or plane's swing off its heading

explanation.surface: A small boat strays from its course line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boat's' is the possessive that hinges the definition onto the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawl is a small two-masted sailing craft, or a ship's dinghy.

clue.text: Bitter cabin crew finally cut out

indicators.note: out means awry or wrong, so the remaining letters are put in a new order
each of the two words has its final letter cut away

explanation.surface: Bitter cabin crew are finally laid off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally cut' removes the last letters of CABIN and CREW (N, W); 'out' rearranges CABICRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbic means sharp and sour in taste or tone, harshly biting.

clue.text: In a month, a lot of potential surrounding island

indicators.note: the potential piece surrounds the island, holding it inside

parts.note: kV, kilovolts, is a lot of potential difference
an isle is an island

explanation.surface: In a month, a great deal of promise builds around an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' looks like promise but is electrical potential, measured in volts.
explanation.definitionFit: Kislev is the ninth month of the Jewish calendar, falling around November and December.

clue.text: Ingredient of Christmas pickle, that's clear

indicators.note: Ingredient of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A seasonal pickle has an ingredient that is clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ingredient' sounds culinary, as aspic is, but signals letters inside christmAS PICkle.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a clear savoury jelly made from stock, used to set meats and eggs.

clue.text: Danger Man's back, a light touch around half-nine?

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: sir is a way of addressing a man

indicators.note: the light touch goes around the half-nine, enclosing it

parts.note: a kiss is a light touch of the lips

indicators.note: half of a word is half its letters, here its second half, the last two letters

explanation.surface: Danger Man returns: a gentle touch at half past nine?
explanation.walkthrough: Danger Man was a 1960s British TV spy series. 'half-nine' looks like a time but gives the second half of NINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Riskiness is the quality of being risky, exposed to hazard and peril.

clue.text: Briefly conceal what makes for a slippery slope

definitions.text: what makes for a slippery slope

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to screen something is to hide it from view

explanation.surface: A quick cover-up leads to a slippery slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slippery slope' is usually a figure of speech about morals; here it is literal loose rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Scree is loose broken rock on a mountainside, notoriously slippery to walk on.

clue.text: Gas almost left in property

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly

explanation.surface: Gas has almost been left inside a building.
explanation.walkthrough: CHATTE, CHATTER without its last letter, then L.
explanation.definitionFit: A chattel is an item of movable personal property, as in goods and chattels.

clue.text: Mark again needs relative — second son

parts.note: Abel was the second son of Adam and Eve

explanation.surface: Mark, once more, needs a relative: a second son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name but is the verb meaning label.
explanation.definitionFit: To relabel is to put a new tag or label on something, marking it once more.

clue.text: US agency initially sent in to hide Republican immorality

indicators.note: the first letter goes in the other word, within its letters

parts.note: to secrete something is to hide it away

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: vice is immoral behaviour

explanation.surface: A US agency is first sent in to cover up a Republican's misconduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hide' is the verb SECRETE, which takes in the first letter of 'sent' before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Secret Service is the American federal agency that guards the president.
